dockerfile_lines: # Bundle the web app so the deployment serves it at / (docs/INSTALLATION.md).
# The build is made for http.mount_prefix from langgraph.json, so the UI's asset URLs and router match where the server mounts it.
# Best effort: a failed UI build leaves the backend deployable without the bundled UI.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends build-essential && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
COPY package.json pnpm-lock.yaml pnpm-workspace.yaml turbo.json langgraph.json /tmp/web-src/
# pnpm hashes every patchedDependencies file on install, even ones outside the filtered packages.
# The web app build bakes SOURCE_COMMIT into the bundle's compile-time constants and its sidecar; the backend stamps its own sidecar from the same value.
# These lines run before the source copy, so the backend sidecar goes to a location created here and read at runtime, not into the openswe package.

RUN ( set -e && export SOURCE_COMMIT && apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl xz-utils ca-certificates && arch=$(uname -m) && case $arch in x86_64) node_arch=x64;; aarch64) node_arch=arm64;; *) echo unsupported arch $arch; exit 1;; esac && curl -fsSL https://nodejs.org/dist/v24.20.0/node-v24.20.0-linux-$node_arch.tar.xz | tar -xJ -C /usr/local --strip-components=1 && corepack enable && cd /tmp/web-src && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --filter open-swe-dashboard... && export WEB_BASE_PATH="$(python3 -c 'import json; print(json.load(open("langgraph.json")).get("http", {}).get("mount_prefix") or "")')/" && pnpm --filter open-swe-dashboard run build && mkdir -p /opt/open-swe-dashboard && cp -R ui/.output/public/. /opt/open-swe-dashboard/ ) || echo 'web build failed; continuing without the bundled UI'; rm -rf /tmp/web-src /usr/local/lib/node_modules /usr/local/bin/node /usr/local/bin/corepack /usr/local/bin/npm /usr/local/bin/npx /usr/local/bin/pnpm /usr/local/bin/pnpx /root/.cache /root/.local/share/pnpm /var/lib/apt/lists/*
